01 — The question

Where does a growing city go?

Urban growth needs land, and city edges often sit on fertile farmland. Digital mapping shows how land cover changes so we can plan better.

Urban edge
🌾 🌾 🌾 🌾

Farm → City

Homes, roads, offices and warehouses replace or fragment crop fields at the urban edge.

The toolkit
🛰️GISDATAMAP

Pixels become evidence.

Satellites photograph the same land again and again. AI sorts each pixel into crops, buildings, trees or water, so years can be compared.

Why it matters
🌱

Land is more than a plot.

Farmland supports food security, farmer livelihoods, groundwater recharge, biodiversity and cooler, less flood-prone cities.

Think about solutions →

03 — The evidence

Maps that make the change visible.

Uploaded land-cover maps are presented as visual evidence. The numeric Rewari land-use figures below come from a published 2024 remote-sensing study.

VISUAL EVIDENCE • INDIA

Land cover is not static.

The submitted map screenshots show the spatial pattern of agricultural, vegetated and built-up surfaces across India. Use the cards to inspect the evidence images at full size.

Satellite / GIS visualisationLand-cover mappingIndia context

LAND AREA • REWARI CITY

Published land-use values, 1989 → 2020.

Source: Kanav et al., Journal of Landscape Ecology, 2024
YearAgricultural land (km²)Built-up land (km²)Built-up share
198911.411.837.30%
20009.703.2312.88%
201111.055.5222.02%
20204.7614.7258.73%
Key result: Rewari's built-up area rose from 1.83 km² in 1989 to 14.72 km² in 2020 — a reported 704% increase. Agricultural land fell from 11.41 km² to 4.76 km² over the same study period.
Important: These figures are for the Rewari City study area and are not India-wide totals. They are published classification results, so they should not be presented as Google Earth Engine/Dynamic World measurements for 2017–2024.

04 — Data snapshot

India, in numbers.

Research highlights from NRSC/ISRO and the Rewari case study.

annual LULC mapping cycles, 2005–06 to 2022–23.

NRSC ANALYSIS23.4 pp

Combined contribution of the five agriculture-related classes to mapped built-up increase.

REWARI STUDY704%

Reported increase in built-up area, 1989 to 2020.

Where did the built-up increase come from? (percentage points)

Source: NRSC Annual Land Use and Land Cover Atlas of India, 2005–06 to 2022–23. The 23.4 pp figure is the sum of the five agriculture-related classes (6.3 + 5.8 + 5.3 + 3.1 + 2.9); wasteland is not agricultural land. Values are contributions to mapped built-up increase, not shares of India's total farmland.

05 — Case study

Rewari: a closer look.

A 2024 study examined Rewari City using open-source Landsat data, GIS-based unsupervised classification and landscape metrics for 1989–2020.

704%built-up increase
12.8%annual expansion rate
69.4%of increase at the expense of vegetation + farmland

⚠ These figures are Rewari-specific, not India-wide.

08 — Possible action

Map it. Plan it. Protect it.

Digital mapping gives planners and researchers spatial evidence for land-use decisions.

🧭

Smart planning

Grow compactly and use existing urban land before fertile farmland.

🛰️

Monitor change

Repeat satellite mapping to catch rapid land-cover shifts early.

🌾

Value farmland

Recognise the food, water and livelihood value of agricultural land.

📢

Build awareness

Turn technical GIS findings into visuals people understand.

Development is necessary, but it should not come at the cost of food security, fertile soil and ecological balance.
